instantiation.worst_case: If the grant is wrong, hello (namespace hello, ClusterIP only, gateways: [mesh], no internet exposure) either admits a principal it should not — one idempotent read-only method, /hello.v1.HelloService/Hello, returning "hello <name>" with no persisted data and no downstream dependency — or keeps denying frontend, in which case frontend's unimplemented Home handler keeps returning Unimplemented. Identifiers derived from deploy/base (namespace, pod labels, container name) and confirmed against the fleet and live metrics; stack lines discovered from the metrics backend's family list and the platform's manifests, each with a cheap re-verification query.

summary: May ship with eyes open. The generated grant is correct and narrow: principal, namespace label, pod label, port 50051 and the method path all match the caller's real manifests and live pods, the platform stamp verifies, and three new e2e checks prove the grant, an identity-based denial and survival of a node drain on every pull request. Two things to see first: a grpcurl load-generator Deployment in namespace frontend already holds ServiceAccount frontend, so the grant admits it too; and the policy lives in deploy/base, reaching e1-dev and e1-prod in one sync with no staged judgment and no alerting rules loaded anywhere to notice. Prod has no metrics, so its side is manifest-only.
